property_summary: For any depositor and deposit amount > MinDeposit, the reference contract increases balances by the exact msg.value and after a subsequent CashOut of some amount the stored balance for that depositor equals the original increased balance minus the cashed out amount; the mutant instead caps increases to MinDeposit so for some deposits this equality breaks.

For any depositor and any deposit > MinDeposit, the reference contract increases balances by the full msg.value (so after CashOut the stored balance equals previous_balance + msg.value - cashed_amount); the mutant instead adds only MinDeposit, so there exist values (msg.value > MinDeposit) where balances differ after CashOut.

For any depositor and any deposit amount > MinDeposit, after depositing and then cashing out some amount not exceeding their balance, the contract's balances mapping for that depositor equals previous_balance + msg.value - cashed_amount (the reference adds full msg.value on Deposit, while the mutant caps the increase to MinDeposit and thus can produce a different stored balance after CashOut).

For any depositor address A and deposit value v > MinDeposit and any cashout amount x ≤ resulting balance, after performing Deposit(v) then CashOut(x) the reference contract's stored balances(A) equals previous_balance + v - x; the mutant that adds only MinDeposit instead of msg.value will violate this for some v > MinDeposit (so there exists fuzzed inputs where balances differ after CashOut).

For any depositor address A and any deposit value v strictly greater than MinDeposit, if A deposits v then cashes out an amount x ≤ resulting balance, the reference contract's balances(A) after CashOut equals previous_balance + v - x (it adds full msg.value), whereas the mutant that caps additions to MinDeposit can make balances(A) larger in the reference than in the mutant for some v and x.

For any caller and any sent value, the reference contract increases the caller's balances when msg.value > MinDeposit; the mutant may fail to do so for some inputs because it adds an extra msg.value != 0 check (allowing a different observable balances outcome for some fuzzed values).

For any caller and any sent amount, if Deposit is called with msg.value > MinDeposit then the contract's balances for the caller increases by that msg.value (i.e. c.balances(caller) after == before + amount); the mutant's added `msg.value != 0` can prevent this for msg.value == 0 (or otherwise change behavior for zero), so the property is that when amount > MinDeposit the balance increases by amount — the mutant breaks this for some inputs.
